1. Detect the song tempo

Start by automatically detecting the song BPM.
You can then adjust the grid if needed.

2. Enable the grid

Turn on “Grid”, then adjust it if needed with “Sync”.
This lets you work correctly in time.

Tip:
place the playhead on a beat of the song, then press “Sync”.

This will automatically realign the grid to the song beats.

A well-aligned grid makes the following much easier:
• loops
• segments
• structures
• future assemblies

3. Define a zone (IN / OUT)

Place:
• an IN point
• an OUT point

to isolate a specific part of the song precisely.

You can immediately test the loop to fine-tune your points accurately.

4. Create segments

Once your zones are defined, create segments such as:
• intro
• verse
• chorus
• solo
• outro
etc.

These segments will be used to build your arrangements.

Tip:
“-” mode is very useful for removing part of a song,
for example:
• a chorus
• a verse
• an intro that is too long

5. Organize the structure

Arrange your segments in the desired order to create:
• a short version
• a live version
• a medley
• a custom structure

6. Edit quickly

The structure remains fully editable:
• move
• replace
• delete
• reorganize

You can try different ideas very quickly.

7. Test your arrangement

Start Structure playback to check:
• transitions
• segment flow
• the overall rhythm of the song

8. 🎯 Final assembly

“Assemble” button:

• creates the final song
• ready to be used live in your library
